thread:
Eva M.: Hey team — addressed the review comments on PR #3421 (runtime batching edge case). Split the large refactor into two commits, fixed the flaky test, and added a short changelog entry. PTAL when you have a moment. planning to merge tomorrow morning if there are no blockers.
Sam H.: thanks! quick q — did you adjust the batcher timeout we discussed?
Eva M.: yep bumped it from 20s -> 45s in tests/runtime/test_batch.py (inline):
```py
# tests/runtime/test_batch.py
BATCH_TIMEOUT = 45  # increased to reduce flake on slow CI workers
```
Sam H.: cool. did you try a local stress run?
Eva M.: ran 1000 short requests locally, KV cache looks stable. left one TODO about a log level.
Jonathan L.: one nit: logging line still uses fstring, can we use logger.debug rather than print? small but helps trace.
Eva M.: good catch — updated to logger.debug and adjusted message to include request_id. pushed.
Luis R.: CI shows an integration flake in the gpu-queue job, reran that workflow.
ci-bot: Re-run requested by Luis R. — gpu-queue (rerun #2)
ci-bot: gpu-queue passed — all checks green ✅
Kevin (CI): LGTM from infra side. Can we hold merge until after a quick canary? I'd prefer a 2-hour canary on dedicated to watch latency.
Eva M.: putting a canary schedule in the PR description: canary at 9:00 AM PST tomorrow for ~2h, will monitor dashboards and echo any regressions.
Sam H.: tiny request: add a brief note in the changelog pointing to the batching perf dashboard so PMs can see the numbers.
Eva M.: added changelog link: https://internal.redwood.dev/changelog#3421 and perf dashboard link in PR description.
Jonathan L.: approved.
Luis R.: approved.
Kevin (CI): approved from infra side — merge window OK after canary.
Eva M.: planning to merge after 11:00 PST if no issues during canary. thanks everyone for the quick reviews :tada:
